7. Developer Pain Points

  • MCP OAuth is the biggest cluster today — Windows broker caches (#5236), ACP refresh-token bypass (#5229), token resend loops (#5233), and unusable TUIs on auth-required servers (#5234). The unified theme: refresh tokens exist but aren't used, and auth states don't persist across processes.
  • Agent permission bypasses — Hooks not firing for sub-agents (#3013) and trusted-folder auto-approval (#5232) erode confidence in the permission model. Both framed explicitly as security issues.
  • Custom agent config not honored — Model and reasoning-effort frontmatter silently ignored (#5241), and unknown model IDs cause prompt-budget failures that wedge sessions (#5219). Combined with plugin agent MCP cancellations (#5237), custom agents feel second-class.
  • Configuration parity gaps — Settings respected in one mode but ignored in another (includeCoAuthoredBy in ACP, sandbox flags pre-1.0.103). Users are effectively re-discovering which mode honors which setting.
  • Environment fragility — Proxy-only web_fetch DNS failures (#5230), Linux sandbox DNS with systemd-resolved (recently fixed, #5027), and inotify budget exhaustion (#5242) show the CLI struggles in constrained enterprise/container environments.
  • Cost and context surprises — The 50-image cache limit triggers full cache refills on each eviction after image 51 (#5238), producing "very, very expensive" sessions.
  • Regressions on the bleeding edge — Voice segfault since 1.0.100 (#5197) and macOS TTY breakage (#5240) reinforce the stable-channel ask.

Digest generated from github.com/github/copilot-cli activity on 2026-10-23. Links reflect source issue URLs.

OpenCode — anomalyco/opencode

OpenCode Community Digest — 2026-10-23

1. Today's Highlights

A quiet release day: v1.19.4 is a maintenance bump that upgrades the bundled Bun runtime to 1.4.4, pulling in security fixes across Brotli, TLS, HTTP/1.1–3, WebSocket, and fetch, plus updated root certificates (NSS 3.131.1) — a recommended upgrade for anyone exposing OpenCode over the network. Issue activity remains dominated by the V2 migration: model picker capability gaps, session titling regressions, provider registration failures, and permission-boundary concerns are recurring themes. On the PR side, core maintainer rekram1-node landed a large batch of MCP lifecycle and model-default fixes, while a community PR re-lands Brave Search as a built-in websearch provider.

2. Releases

v1.19.4

Core — Improvements

  • Upgraded the bundled Bun runtime to 1.4.4, which includes security fixes for Brotli, TLS, HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, WebSocket, and fetch
  • Updated root certificates to NSS 3.131.1

No behavioral or API changes in this release — it is a runtime/security maintenance drop.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #2242 — Is there a way to sandbox the agent? (OPEN · 101 comments · 👍 80) The single most-discussed open issue. Users want filesystem confinement for agent terminal commands, comparing against seatbelt in gemini-cli/codex-cli. The sustained comment volume and high reaction count make this the clearest signal for a first-class sandboxing story.

  2. #52083 — Compound shell commands drop redirection, turning an allowed command into an unprompted file write (OPEN · 4 comments) A security-relevant permission bypass: the command scanner splits chained commands but omits redirection targets from evaluated resources. Pairs directly with #2242 and should be prioritized regardless of the sandbox roadmap.

  3. #50652 — External plugin tools bypass configured permissions (OPEN · 3 comments · 👍 2) Plugin-registered tools execute without applying their configured permission action, including via Code Mode. Extends the permission-model concerns beyond built-in shell handling.

  4. #50257 — Desktop model picker shows "No reasoning" for all V2 models (OPEN · 15 comments) capabilities.reasoning is never set, so the tooltip mislabels every reasoning-capable V2 model. Cosmetic but highly visible; 15 comments indicate broad impact across the desktop user base.

  5. #51828 — Location inactivity eviction SIGTERMs live background shells after 60 minutes (OPEN · 6 comments) locations.invalidate() tears down the location-scoped Shell/Pty graph while the service process stays alive. Long-running background work dies silently — a serious correctness issue for agentic workflows.

  6. #58176 — Session titles never generated in v2 (OPEN · 3 comments · reproduced) No auto-trigger plus free-tier rejection means new sessions stay "Untitled session," a clear regression from v1.18.x. Low-severity individually, but a visible quality regression for all V2 users.

  7. #58335 — Console account connected but opencode provider never registers (CLOSED · 3 comments) Console returns 52 models, yet /api/provider omits opencode and /api/model has zero opencode/* entries. A blocker for Console users on v2.1.3.

  8. #47646 — ChatGPT OAuth reports 400k context for long-context models (CLOSED · 15 comments) OpenCode overwrites effective context limits (~1.05M catalog) with 400,000 tokens, causing the TUI to overstate headroom and degrade compaction decisions. Now closed, but high engagement.

  9. #56783 — V2: compaction fires on first request / loops when compaction.buffer ≥ context limit (CLOSED · 2 comments · reproduced) Misconfiguration produces meaningless structured summaries at session start and repeating Session… internal errors. Worth a guard/validation in config loading.

  10. #58327 — Custom websearch providers cannot signal rate limits + #58328 — Re-land Brave as a built-in provider (OPEN) Two same-day issues from one author: built-in providers participate in 429 → Retry-After → failover, but plugin-registered providers via ctx.websearch.transform have no way to signal throttling. #58328 also flags a process gap — PR #48222 was stale-bot-closed without review.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #58355 — fix(core): use the agent's model when a session has none Honors agents.<id>.model / agent frontmatter for opencode run and run --agent, which previously always used the server default. Fixes a long-standing headless/CLI inconsistency.

  2. #58352 — fix(core): default to agent and last used model when none is selected Prevents opencode run from silently landing on the newest released model across all providers (currently opencode/flint-40b-free) — a real cost-correctness fix for paid users.

  3. #58351 — fix(core): stop MCP servers in parallel on shutdown Serial shutdown cost 2–4s per uncooperative local server, blowing the ~5s restart budget. Fixes #50758.

  4. #58350 — fix(core): skip malformed MCP tools instead of failing the server Validates each tool individually so one bad inputSchema no longer fails the whole tools/list and marks the server as failed at connect time.

  5. #58349 — fix(core): don't duplicate MCP servers started during initial reconciliation Fixes a startup race where a queued launch still runs after connect()/disconnect() completes, spawning a second copy. Fixes #52741.

  6. #58342 — fix(core): keep MCP OAuth login waiting after stray callback requests Loopback callback no longer treats code-less requests (e.g. Chrome PNA preflights) as fatal auth failures. Fixes #55201 and unblocks Chrome-on-Linux MCP auth.

  7. #58341 — fix(core): keep remote MCP requests open past Bun's fetch idle timeout Remote MCP calls silent >5 min now survive instead of failing at Bun's idle timeout, far ahead of OpenCode's 12h MCP execution timeout.

  8. #58344 — fix(ai): fold long Mistral-family tool call IDs over the whole ID (and related #58339) Mistral's 9-char ID cap was truncating rather than folding, causing prefix collisions for GLM and other models behind mistral-prefixed routes. Fixes #58323.

  9. #58334 — feat(core): add Brave web search Re-lands #48222 (Brave as a built-in websearch provider) after the original was closed by stale-PR automation without review. Closes #58328.

  10. #58346 — fix(core): refresh DigitalOcean routers while signed in Restores router discovery mid-session (removed in #57175 to stop signed-out polling) without re-introducing the every-5-minutes-everywhere behavior.

Also worth watching: #58343 — fix(desktop): follow up dev server split (dev-channel builds get their own DB; adds a Home hint for migrating dogfooders), #57470 — clipboard images via Windows interop on WSL, and #58347 — use /usr/local/etc/opencode on FreeBSD.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussions data was provided in the source material; this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilled from Issues and PRs updated in the last 24h:

  • Agent sandboxing and permissions hardening — #2242 (sandbox mode), #52083 (redirect bypass), #50652 (plugin permission bypass). This is now a cluster, not a single ask, and the top comment/reaction issue overall.
  • Websearch provider flexibility — #58327 and #58328 both target the same subsystem: custom providers need rate-limit signaling, and built-in Brave should be re-landed.
  • Model/execution configuration surface — #58330 requests a model execution location toggle alongside existing API key permissions; #54881 requests a root session ID header on LLM requests for sub-agent attribution.
  • Usage observability — #57975 proposes a unified real-time usage dashboard across all AI models, motivated by unclear free-tier limits; #58014 reports free-limit exhaustion after only a few requests, suggesting the demand is partly driven by counting ambiguity.
  • UI/UX polish — #58034 (configurable timestamp format in desktop/web), #51868 (unreviewed zh machine translations plus 93 missing keys of 1828), #56109 (Windows /cd tab-completion appends backslash).

7. Developer Pain Points

  • V2 migration regressions dominate the issue tracker. Session titling (#58176), provider registration (#58335), compaction loops (#56783), and model capability display (#50257) are all V2-specific and all user-visible. Several are already labeled reproduced.
  • Permission model is inconsistent across surfaces. Built-in shell, plugin tools, and Code Mode each behave differently; #52083 and #50652 both describe silent bypasses. Trust in the permission system is the underlying complaint, not any single bug.
  • MCP lifecycle is fragile at the edges. Startup duplication (#58349), serial shutdown stalls (#58351), malformed-tool server failure (#58350), OAuth callback misclassification (#55201), and Bun fetch idle timeouts (#58341) are five distinct failure modes on one subsystem — the same-day cluster of core PRs reads as a deliberate hardening pass.
  • Documentation/catalog drift. #55904 (retired Exo and MiMo V2.5 models still advertised), #50405 (location vs path in the plugins guide), and #51868 (untranslated/mistranslated zh strings) share a root cause: docs and locale catalogs lag the shipping product.
  • Process friction in the contribution pipeline. #58328 explicitly calls out a fully implemented PR (#48222) that was closed by stale-bot automation without ever being reviewed on its merits — a case where the review process, not the code, is the bottleneck.
  • Windows/FreeBSD platform gaps. #56109 (backslash on /cd completion), #57470 (WSL clipboard), and #58347 (FreeBSD config path) show non-macOS/Linux platforms still need targeted fixes rather than falling out of the main development loop.
Pi — earendil-works/pi

Pi Community Digest — 2026-10-23

1. Today's Highlights

Today's activity is dominated by a cluster of TUI/performance and correctness fixes landing in quick succession: HTML export stack-overflow fixes, fuzzy-search ranking improvements, and macOS shell-group termination races all got PRs. Meanwhile, the startup-time budget debate (#7739) continues as the most-commented open issue, signaling growing competitive pressure from rival harnesses like jcode. A notable cluster of closed-as-no-action issues (HTML comment stripping, /reload for AGENTS.md, MCP OAuth client names) suggests maintainers are triaging aggressively but declining scope creep.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. [#7739 OPEN] Startup-time budget targeting jcode-comparable latency and memory — 11 comments The single most active issue. Proposes a formal startup-time budget for Pi, benchmarked against jcode v0.9.1888-dev. This is a strategic signal: the community is treating competitor benchmarks as a north star. Worth watching for roadmap impact. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7739

  2. [#6167 CLOSED] transformMessages thinking-block normalization vs. requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages — 10 comments A subtle compatibility-flag interaction bug that took months to resolve. Demonstrates how fragile cross-provider reasoning-content handling remains as a class of bugs. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/6167

  3. [#9932 OPEN] before_agent_start forced system prompt keeps removed tools — 6 comments Extension lifecycle ordering bug: setActiveTools() removals are lost when a system prompt is forced. High-value for extension authors building constrained agents. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9932

  4. [#10259 OPEN] Public tool-presentation API or one-line tool mode — 5 comments, 👍2 Requests a display-only API to control all tool rows (built-ins, MCP, codemode, custom). Strong extension-ecosystem signal. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10259

  5. [#11223 OPEN] modelOverrides silently ignored for classifier models — 5 comments Config silently ignored — a dangerous class of bug. Users discover it only when behavior doesn't match docs. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11223

  6. [#9807 OPEN] TUI full re-render causes scroll/typing lag at 800+ messages — 5 comments, 👍3 Performance regression with high user agreement. Root cause is lack of incremental cell-level diffing (contrasted with OpenCode's OpenTUI). https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9807

  7. [#11086 OPEN, prio:p0] Symbols leaking into input on Windows terminal under CPU load — 4 comments P0-tagged input corruption. Nasty reproducibility profile (SSH + client CPU load) makes it hard to chase but high-impact. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11086

  8. [#11259 CLOSED] WSL bracketed-paste from Windows Terminal drops image paste — 3 comments Closed, but representative of the growing WSL/Windows interop pain surface. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11259

  9. [#11172 OPEN] Split mouse report tail leaks into prompt — 2 comments Escape-timeout half-flush bug in StdinBuffer. Low comment count but a clean minimal repro that likely affects editor input robustness broadly. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11172

  10. [#11253 OPEN, fix-available] forkFrom writes one appendFileSync per entry — 2 comments 73 MB / 3,322-entry session took >30s to fork, breaking host handshake. "Fix available" tag means maintainer bandwidth is the only blocker. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11253

4. Key PR Progress

  1. [#11309 OPEN] Await extension user messages — muyiyr Returns the underlying promise from extension sendUserMessage so command handlers can await the generated turn. Includes a regression test for #11238. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11309

  2. [#11304 OPEN] Start when a configured package fails to install — Lincoln504 Prevents a bad package from aborting startup; failures surface via the extension warning channel. Big resilience win for multi-package setups. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11304

  3. [#11296 CLOSED] Rank contiguous fuzzy matches; search session fields separately — petrroll Fixes the /model opus ranking weirdness (#11220) and closes three related issues. Changes fuzzy scoring to prefer contiguous, substring-aligned matches. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11296

  4. [#11293 CLOSED] Render HTML export for sessions deeper than the call stack — petrroll Replaces recursive tree walks in the export viewer with iterative stacks. Long sessions no longer render blank. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11293

  5. [#11290 CLOSED] Render system messages in HTML export — petrroll Fixes #11261: system entries (initial prompt and section updates) now appear in exports, plus CLI --export surfaces prompt and tools. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11290

  6. [#11289 CLOSED] Stop macOS shell groups before killing them — petrroll Closes the abort-race (#11252) where a; b could still run b. Linux/Windows paths unchanged; kill fallbacks preserved. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11289

  7. [#11288 OPEN] Write forked session through one fd — robopipi[bot] Fixes the O(N) open/close on forkFrom for large sessions (#11253). Bot-authored but touches a real correctness/perf issue. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11288

  8. [#11278 CLOSED] Preserve ctx.ui getters through wrapUIPromptContext — ljm15913101281 Object-spread was evaluating get theme() at bind time, breaking late theme initialization in hosts like pi-web. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11278

  9. [#11275 CLOSED] Avoid deep export tree stack overflow — muyiyr Parallel fix to #11293; landed the same day with a 20,000-entry regression test. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/11275

  10. [#10528 OPEN] Refactor Nix packaging — ReStranger Slims package.nix (drop *.map, *.d.ts), uses makeBinaryWrapper, skips version check under Nix. Still open, worth tracking for the Nix distribution. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/10528

5. Hot Discussions

Show and tell

  • [#11307] pi-better-web-search — one web_search tool, raw provider results, real cross-provider fallback Extracts the web-search tool from pi-web-search to fix two gripes: rewritten results and no fallback when the current model can't search. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/discussions/11307

  • [#11306] pi-continuity — auto-resume after coding-plan usage limits and interrupted turns Automates the "come back in 5 hours and type continue" loop for OpenAI 5-hour limits. Complements existing transient-error retries and compaction. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/discussions/11306

(No Ideas or Q&A discussions in the last 24h.)

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Extension observability & presentation APIs — #10259 (public tool-presentation API), #11090 (preserve model attribution for auxiliary token usage), #7828 (message identity in markdown transformer context). Extension authors want deeper hooks with less guessing.
  • Startup / runtime performance — #7739 (startup budget vs. jcode), #9807 (TUI re-render lag), #11253 ("fix-available" fork slowness). Perf is now a competitive narrative, not just polish.
  • Cross-harness compatibility & config fidelity — #11250/#11251 (HTML comment stripping to match Claude Code), #10226 (MCP OAuth client name), #11223 (modelOverrides honoring). Users want Pi to behave the way other tools do.
  • Session lifecycle control — #11292/#11291 (reload AGENTS.md mid-session), #11295 (provider-scoped auto-compaction with absolute thresholds). Fine-grained control over what's loaded and when.
  • Auto-compaction configurability — #11295 and related discussion of per-provider thresholds.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Input/terminal edge cases dominate bug reports. Windows symbol leakage under CPU load (#11086), WSL bracketed-paste image drops (#11259), split-escape mouse reports (#11172), macOS abort races (#11252). The TUI input layer is the highest-friction surface.
  • Silent failures erode trust. modelOverrides ignored (#11223), missing checkpointWhen crashing only at first commit (#11305), uncaught No API provider registered mid-session (#11287). Errors that don't surface until much later are the most painful class.
  • Long sessions break rendering and forking. Stack overflows in HTML export (#11225), full re-renders in TUI (#9807), and O(N) forkFrom I/O (#11253) all share a root cause: data structures that don't scale past ~1k–3k entries.
  • Extension/agent lifecycle ordering is fragile. #9932 (tool removal lost when forcing system prompt) and #11278 (getters evaluated at bind time) show that init-order assumptions leak into public APIs.
  • Docs vs. reality gaps. #11223 and #11282 both cite docs or the website promising behavior that doesn't match shipped code or public repositories.
  • Triaging pace vs. scope creep. Nine issues closed as [no-action] today alone (HTML comments, /reload, MCP OAuth names) — maintainers are declining small compatibility asks to protect the core, which some contributors will read as "not listening."
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest — 2026-10-23

1. Today's Highlights

A new v0.26.0-nightly.20261022.bf66a26c97 build landed, headlined by daemon token persistence in qwen serve. Meanwhile, the community is converging on session/workspace management as the dominant theme — terminology standardization, per-session working directories, and sidebar UX — alongside a cluster of P1 correctness bugs around truncated tool calls and lost tool results on Windows.

2. Releases

v0.26.0-nightly.20261022.bf66a26c97 (release notes)

  • feat(serve): add daemon token persistence (#15023 by @wenshao) — tokens survive daemon restarts, a prerequisite for durable session management.
  • fix(release): cover every spawned vendored binary — closes a packaging gap where some shipped binaries were not exercised during release verification.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #13078 — Daily dependency CVE audit failed (29 comments, still open since 09-30). The bot-tracked audit keeps failing, suggesting either a persistent high-severity advisory or an unavailable npm audit endpoint. Longest-running thread of the day; worth watching for supply-chain hygiene.

  2. #13787 — XML recovery repeats prefix scans on large multi-call responses. Performance regression with a reproducible benchmark on main; matters because response sizes grow with multi-tool workflows. Community supplied a direct-parser reproduction.

  3. #15165 — Shell safety parser triggers ~1.6 GiB transient WASM allocation on Node 24.16.0. A memory spike from V8 optimizing the bundled Bash WASM parser. High-impact for CI/container users with constrained memory.

  4. #15248 — ci(sdk-java): runtime broker timing tests flake 3/3 on GitHub-hosted runners. Flaky tests block the fork PR fast lane — a contributor-experience problem that directly impedes outside contributions.

  5. #15310 — Tell the model which shell it uses, instead of letting it assume bash. On Windows, Qwen Code uses cmd.exe but the prompt implies POSIX, so commands fail. Simple, high-leverage fix with a clear repro.

  6. #15297 — Qwen Code 0.26.0 loses tool output in ~1 of 40 calls (P1). 43 instances / 1,663 calls, 28 confirmed via transcripts. Tool runs successfully but no functionResponse reaches the model — a serious correctness issue causing forced re-reads.

  7. #15324 — bug(acp): edit truncated by max_tokens is written to disk (P1). A partial write_file is executed and reported as success. Affects Zed, the VS Code companion, and qwen serve — potential data-corruption class bug.

  8. #15327 — tracking(core): run every surface on one agent loop behind experimental.unifiedAgentLoop (P1). Proposes consolidating the duplicated agent loops (Ink vs. OpenTUI vs. ACP). Architecturally significant; see also #15326 below.

  9. #15326 — OpenTUI runs tool calls from a retried attempt and does not record native tool results. Concrete evidence of the divergence #15327 aims to eliminate — the OpenTUI loop is a separate copy in live-session.ts.

  10. #15325 — stream-json message past --max-session-turns returns success with the previous answer. Silent failure mode in SDK transport: no model request, success status, stale answer. SDK clients see this.

Also noteworthy: #15328 (headless exits 0 with no output when truncated) and #15077 (archived session listing + title search, now CLOSED).

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #15211 — feat(serve): carry a scheduled-task gate through the daemon and Web Shell (by @wenshao). Follow-up to #15069; lets scheduled tasks run a gating shell command at each fire. Core to the managed-automation story.

  2. #15218 — feat(managed): gate managed automations on a Runtime probe run before the claim. Quiet-gate semantics (skipped/gate_quiet) settle occurrences without a turn — efficient for no-op fires.

  3. #15323 — feat(serve): allow secondary sessions to cd within their workspace. Implements the sandboxed working-directory model requested in #15316, with realpath containment.

  4. #15283 — feat(cli): align OpenTUI session recovery with Ink. A large batch: owned cancellation, persistent recall, resume/branch replay, rewind, checkpoint restore. Directly addresses the OpenTUI/Ink divergence.

  5. #15255 — feat(managed-agent): shared Harness pool for Kubernetes. Opt-in pooled hosting with placement epochs and writer-grant fencing — a meaningful step toward multi-tenant scale.

  6. #15261 — feat(runtime-broker): HTTP-backed external scratch workers. Pairs with #15247: operator-run HTTP service owns worker placement; the broker persists a deterministic request handle for idempotent retries.

  7. #15256 — fix(ci): reuse open workflow failure issues. Cuts down the noise from bot-filed CI failure issues — a direct response to the volume of Main CI failed reports like #15307.

  8. #15329 — feat(ci): switchable Linux runner fleet (hosted/arm64) via LINUX_RUNNER_FLEET. Gives maintainers an arm64 lane and a cleaner escape hatch than the ECS kill switch.

  9. #15320 + #15319 — Web Shell sidebar reorganization (by @deggs7): move Create group into the workspace ⋮ menu, and promote No-workspace sessions to a peer group. Implements the #14988 / #15312 / #15309 discussions.

  10. #15317 — fix(mods): refuse values nested too deeply to cross the Mod boundary. Adds a 512-level nesting limit for Mod→Qwen Code values, preventing unbounded recursion at the extension boundary.

5. Hot Discussions

No GitHub Discussions data was provided in the source dataset, so this section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Session & workspace lifecycle: archived-session listing/search (#15077, now closed), per-session working directories (#15316, #15323), and Unified Agent Loop (#15327) all point to session management as the roadmap's center of gravity.
  • Web Shell UX & terminology: a coordinated push to standardize on Workspace / 工作区 and Session / 会话 (#14988), relocate Create group (#15312), clarify the No-workspace group (#15309), and render full MCP tool args/results (#15280).
  • MCP modernization: first-class MCP 2026-07-28 + MCP Apps support with the Web Shell as primary host (#8968).
  • Platform distribution & runtime: Managed Agent Runtime Broker #15247, shared Harness pool #15255, and a cluster of runtime-broker work. Significant investment in hosted/multi-tenant execution.
  • Shell environment awareness: #15310 asks the model be told it's on cmd.exe; a small ask with outsized Windows impact.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI flakiness blocks external contributors. The sdk-java broker timing tests flake on GitHub-hosted runners (#15248), and the fork fast lane is explicitly named as blocked. Hosted vs. self-hosted runner divergence is the root cause; #15286, #15289, and #15322 are the maintainer response.
  • Hosted-runner timeouts cascade into test budgets. PRs #15101 and #15183 both rewrite fixed 10s waits to use a slow-host policy — evidence the hosted environment is routinely too slow for the current budgets.
  • Truncation/loss bugs are the sharpest correctness concern. #15297 (silent tool-result loss in 0.26.0), #15324 (truncated write committed to disk), #15325 (stale success past turn limit), and #15328 (exit 0, no output) are four independent silent-failure reports in one day. The common thread: failures are invisible to the caller and reported as success.
  • Windows shell handling remains a rough edge. #15310 (no shell context in prompt) and #15297 (Windows-specific tool-result loss) both hit Windows users disproportionately.
  • Duplicate agent loops create divergent bug surfaces. The OpenTUI loop's behavioral drift (#15326) is the immediate symptom; #15327 is the proposed structural fix.
  • Bot-filed issue noise. Multiple Deferred review findings and Main CI failed issues (#15307) are generated by automation; #15256 (reuse open failure issues) is the mitigation.

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Dự án theo dõi: 5 | Tạo lúc: 2026-10-23 05:33 UTC

Báo cáo chuyên sâu dự án OpenClaw

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-23

1. Tổng quan hôm nay

OpenClaw đang vận hành với thông lượng rất cao hôm nay, với 500 issue và 500 PR được cập nhật trong 24 giờ qua, phản ánh một dự án trưởng thành, có lưu lượng truy cập lớn với maintainer và pipeline triage (bot clawsweeper) tích cực cùng một lượng lớn người dùng tự host. Hoạt động nghiêng về củng cố tính ổn định hơn là tính năng mới: hàng đợi issue chủ yếu là các regression P0/P1 về crash-loop, mất tin nhắn và trạng thái session, trong khi hàng đợi PR chủ yếu do steipete và các maintainer khác gộp các bề mặt nội bộ dùng một consumer, sửa lỗi authority trong khôi phục sau khởi động lại, và cải thiện UI/hiệu năng. Dự án đã phát hành v2026.10.6, với điểm nhấn là việc bắt buộc nâng cấp runtime Node để vá lỗ hổng chứng chỉ TLS — một bản nâng cấp bắt buộc vì lý do bảo mật. Tín hiệu sức khỏe tổng thể: maintainer phản hồi tốt, nhưng vẫn tồn đọng backlog các regression đặc thù theo nền tảng (Windows, macOS sleep/wake) liên tục tái xuất qua các bản phát hành.

2. Phát hành

v2026.10.6 — openclaw 2026.10.6

Điểm nhấn: Runtime Node đã được vá giờ là bắt buộc.

  • Thay đổi phá vỡ tương thích/bắt buộc: OpenClaw giờ yêu cầu Node 24.22.1+ (nhánh 24) hoặc 26.12.1+ (nhánh 26). Các runtime này từ chối chuỗi TLS được ký bằng khóa chứng chỉ bị xâm phạm đã được đề cập trong các bản phát hành bảo mật Node.js tháng 10 năm 2026.
  • Docker: các image chính thức giờ đi kèm Node 24.2x (tương thích với nhánh đã được vá).
  • Lưu ý khi nâng cấp: Các operator đang chạy Node 24.x hoặc 26.x cũ hơn phải nâng cấp Node trước khi cài đặt bản phát hành này, nếu không các chuỗi TLS được ký bằng khóa bị xâm phạm vẫn có thể được chấp nhận. Đây là bản nâng cấp bắt buộc vì lý do bảo mật, không có nội dung tính năng nào được mô tả.

Không có bản phát hành nào khác trong 24 giờ qua.

So sánh chéo hệ sinh thái

Báo cáo so sánh liên dự án — Hệ sinh thái mã nguồn mở Trợ lý AI cá nhân / Agent

Cửa sổ dữ liệu: 2026-10-23 | Dự án: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Tổng quan hệ sinh thái

Năm dự án được phân tích trải rộng trên một phổ trưởng thành rất rộng — từ OpenClaw, dự án chủ lực tự vận hành với thông lượng cao (~500 issue/PR được cập nhật mỗi ngày, bắt buộc nâng cấp runtime do vấn đề bảo mật) cho đến IronClaw đang trong giai đoạn bảo trì gần như đóng băng (tổng cộng 8 mục, chỉ có PR từ Dependabot). Trên toàn hệ sinh thái, chủ đề kỹ thuật chi phối trong tháng 10/2026 là gia cố thay vì mở rộng: khắc phục vòng lặp crash/mất tin nhắn trên Windows và các đường sleep/wake (OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw), thực thi identity/principal-scope trong triển khai đa tenant (ZeroClaw), và độ tin cậy của channel-adapter (QwenPaw, ZeroClaw). Một chủ đề thứ cấp nhưng dai dẳng là quản trị bộ nhớ — ngân sách ghi, mục tiêu promotion, và ranh giới riêng tư — xuất hiện độc lập ở OpenClaw, Hermes và QwenPaw. Các sự kiện bảo mật (Node TLS bị xâm phạm ở OpenClaw; emSign CA ở QwenPaw) đã dẫn đến hai bản phát hành buộc nâng cấp trong vòng 24 giờ, cho thấy vệ sinh chuỗi cung ứng giờ đây là mối quan tâm hàng đầu khi phát hành.

Hermes đang giữa chu kỳ giữa các bản vá ổn định. IronClaw thực tế đang nghỉ ở các công việc do con người dẫn dắt.

3. Vị thế của OpenClaw

Lợi thế so với các dự án cùng nhóm:

  • Thông lượng ở quy mô lớn: 500 issue + 500 PR được cập nhật trong 24h — gấp khoảng 10 lần Hermes và QwenPaw, và khoảng 15 lần ZeroClaw. 259 PR merge/24h là không đối thủ.
  • Hạ tầng triage có kỷ luật: Bot clawsweeper tự động với nhãn impact/severity tạo ra backlog có thể phân tích bằng máy — dấu hiệu trưởng thành mà không dự án nào sánh được.
  • Nhịp độ release engineering: Phát hành bản release có tên tính năng (v2026.10.6) kèm ghi chú migration rõ ràng, trong khi Hermes hoãn ghi chú được chọn lọc sang bản minor tiếp theo (v0.23.0) và QwenPaw/ZeroClaw đang giữa chu kỳ.
  • Độ rộng hệ sinh thái: Plugin trình duyệt, google-meet, Node companion, Teams — bề mặt tích hợp rộng hơn bất kỳ dự án cùng nhóm nào.

Khác biệt về cách tiếp cận kỹ thuật:

  • OpenClaw là kiến trúc nặng nhất / dễ cắm nhất trong nhóm: plugin-generation capture, thiết lập MCP app, xuất bản prepared-runtime, gateway lanes, các pha sidecar asset. Sức mạnh này cũng là điểm yếu — chính độ phức tạp plugin/capture tạo ra tình trạng tắc event-loop P0 (#160959) và hồi quy khởi động trên Windows (#168955) mà các dự án gọn nhẹ hơn không có.
  • Hermes và QwenPaw chia sẻ mô hình gateway/plugin của OpenClaw nhưng với ít tầng kiến trúc hơn; ZeroClaw đánh đổi độ rộng lấy thiết kế ưu tiên bảo mật theo principal-scope; IronClaw là một artifact nhỏ hơn dựa trên Rust/Cranelift.

So sánh quy mô cộng đồng:

  • OpenClaw rõ ràng là tham chiếu của cả hạng mục — số bình luận issue (43 ở #160959, 27 ở #42475) và các luồng thảo luận vận hành lâu dài cho thấy một cộng đồng người dùng power-user tự vận hành lớn, chạy hàng trăm agent (ví dụ: triển khai ~810 agent). Các dự án cùng nhóm vận hành ở mức ~1/10 lượng người tham gia.
  • Tuy nhiên, xét theo cường độ reaction, Hermes vượt trội so với quy mô của mình: #18715 có 👍42, cao hơn bất kỳ mục OpenClaw nào trong bộ dữ liệu hôm nay — gợi ý một cộng đồng nhỏ hơn nhưng gắn bó về mặt ý tưởng hơn.

Triển khai tối giản / headless ZeroClaw (#11971, #11969), OpenClaw (chỉ CLI), IronClaw (triển khai ARM64) Bản build chỉ CLI, cô lập feature-flag để ngăn gateway lẫn vào artifact headless

Tín hiệu: Bốn trong năm dự án độc lập nêu bật quản trị bộ nhớ và thực thi phạm vi quyền. Những điều này đang hội tụ thành yêu cầu tối thiểu bắt buộc, không còn là điểm khác biệt.

Hermes Agent — Bản tin dự án

Ngày: 2026-10-23 | Repo: github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent

1. Tổng quan hôm nay

Hermes Agent tiếp tục duy trì tốc độ hoạt động cao: 50 issue và 50 PR được cập nhật trong 24 giờ qua, với 15 PR đã merge/đóng và 35 PR vẫn đang mở. Một bản patch (v0.22.5) đã gom khoảng 81 PR đã merge vào một tag ổn định trước thềm v0.23.0. Đáng chú ý, không có issue nào được đóng hôm nay so với 50 issue đang hoạt động — backlog mở tiếp tục tăng nhanh hơn tốc độ xử lý, và phần lớn hoạt động hôm nay tập trung vào các báo cáo lỗi liên quan đến lộ trình cập nhật v0.22.x và độ ổn định của gateway (lỗi cập nhật trên Windows, khôi phục phiên, crash khi compaction). Tốc độ phát triển của chính dự án ("hàng nghìn commit mỗi tuần") giờ đây cũng trở thành một chủ đề lặp lại trong cộng đồng, xuất hiện cả dưới dạng yêu cầu tính năng (tự động sửa lỗi khi cập nhật) lẫn nguyên nhân gốc của cụm lỗi liên quan đến cập nhật.

Đánh giá sức khỏe dự án: Đà phát triển tính năng rất mạnh (model media FAL mới, delegation, kanban), nhưng chất lượng bản phát hành và độ ổn định của cơ chế cập nhật là tín hiệu rủi ro chính trong tuần này.

Nhu cầu cốt lõi: heuristic phê duyệt cần một lớp nghiêm ngặt hơn cho các lệnh tự động hóa OS / có tính phá hủy.

Đây là yêu cầu kiến trúc tách rời, xuất phát từ nhu cầu về quyền riêng tư và phân bổ compute.

IronClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-23

1. Tổng quan hôm nay

IronClaw cho thấy hoạt động ở mức trung bình, thiên về bảo trì trong hôm nay: tổng cộng 8 mục được cập nhật trong 24 giờ qua (2 issue, 6 PR), không có bản phát hành mới. Hoạt động trong ngày chủ yếu là các đợt bump dependency của Dependabot (5 trong 6 PR), cho thấy một giai đoạn phát triển tính năng khá yên ắng, tập trung vào dọn dẹp thay vì công việc tạo ra năng lực mới. Việc đóng issue về hỗ trợ ARM64 Docker đã tồn tại từ lâu (#3168, mở từ tháng 5/2026) là tín hiệu đáng chú ý nhất trong ngày, dù đáng lưu ý rằng nó được đóng mà không có merge nào liên kết. Kết luận: Các đóng hôm nay chủ yếu là ổn định v0.8.7 và vệ sinh bảo mật/CI, trong khi các tính năng v0.9.0 vẫn đang trong quá trình xử lý.

4. Chủ đề cộng đồng nổi bật

Mục Loại Bình luận Chủ đề
#7432 Tracker (p2, rủi ro cao) 15 Lộ trình runtime / đăng nhập dashboard / phân phối gateway
#10526 RFC (p2, rủi ro cao) 13 Lịch sử phiên dựa trên sự kiện & phát lại xác định
#10999 Task bị chặn (trung bình) 9 Cài đặt/xác minh plugin Discord từ binary phát hành
#8279 Bug (p1, rủi ro cao) 5 delegate bỏ qua allowlist công cụ của parent

Phân tích nhu cầu ẩn sau:

  • #7432 là issue điều phối chính cho bản phát hành runtime/gateway v0.9.0 — chuỗi 15 bình luận của nó báo hiệu cuộc tranh luận liên tục về thứ tự và một đồ thị phụ thuộc lớn. Các bên liên quan muốn rõ ràng về những gì sẽ ra mắt trong v0.9.0.
  • Việc đóng #10526 sau cuộc thảo luận RFC kéo dài phản ánh một dự án đang trưởng thành, sẵn sàng tái kiến trúc lưu trữ xung quanh các sự kiện chỉ ghi thêm — dấu hiệu của đầu tư thiết kế dài hạn, dù công việc "luồng agent dẫn xuất" sẽ sinh ra các tracker tiếp theo.
  • #10999 ở trạng thái status:blocked dù đã xác minh Discord hoạt động trên v0.8.6 báo hiệu ma sát về đóng gói/kỹ thuật phát hành (chứng minh một plugin hoạt động từ kho lưu trữ phát hành, không phải từ source).
  • #8279 là lá cờ đầu về bảo mật: lỗ hổng bypass allowlist của delegate thuộc lớp S0 và p1, và nó kết nối trực tiếp với các PR xếp chồng (#11225, #11409, #11230) đã được làm mới trong nhiều tuần.

Các PR được bình luận nhiều nhất là chồng bảo mật của IftekharUddin và Aarlington (#11225 p0, #11409, #11220, #11230, #11234) và nền tảng Goal Mode #11878 — những thứ này dẫn dắt lộ trình hiển thị.

5. Bug & Ổn định

Xếp hạng theo mức độ nghiêm trọng (tất cả được báo cáo/cập nhật 2026-10-22–23):

Mức độ Issue Mô tả PR sửa?
S1 #11957 Đăng ký OIDC gửi thông tin xác thực client thô trong header Basic; ký tự dành riêng phá vỡ đăng ký client_credentials & device-grant ✅ #11968 mở (form-encode thông tin xác thực)
S0/S1 #8279 delegate cho phép sub-agent gọi các công cụ mà chính sách của parent loại trừ ✅ Được bao phủ bởi các PR xếp chồng #11225 / #11409
S2 #11951 Nâng cấp WebSocket của Gateway thất bại trên listener TLS tích hợp (101 rồi đóng) ❌ Chưa có
S2 #11962 64 phiên RPC trực tiếp của Daemon không bao giờ được giải phóng khi nhàn rỗi → client từ xa có thể làm cạn kiệt chúng ✅ #11964 mở ("retire orphaned remote sessions")
S2 #11970 agents delete/rename bỏ qua cascade trạng thái sở hữu + kiểm tra live-ACP trong bản build không có gateway ❌
S2 #11989 excluded_tools theo kênh không bao giờ được áp dụng ✅ #11990 mở
S2 #11991 Email đi HTML chứa markup thô / URL hình ảnh tùy ý (lớp XSS) ❌ (tính năng #11992 liền kề)
S2 #11823 Shell scanner bỏ qua command substitution trong heredoc có delimiter không trích dẫn (thoát sandbox) ❌
S3 #11972 gateway get-paircode thoát với mã 0 khi thất bại ❌
S3 #11969 Các tính năng metrics / embedded-web biên dịch toàn bộ gateway vào bản build headless ✅ #11269 mở
S3 #11987 Bình luận // nosemgrep inline không chặn cảnh báo quét mã ❌

Đánh giá ổn định: Hai bug thuộc lớp thoát sandbox/bảo mật vẫn còn mở (#11823, #11991) mà không có PR sửa — những cái này cần được ưu tiên. Bug đăng ký #11957 là S1 (quy trình bị chặn) nhưng bản sửa đã trong quá trình xem xét. Sự cố WebSocket TLS (#11951) là một vấn đề có dạng regression ảnh hưởng đến khả năng sử dụng dashboard.

6. Yêu cầu tính năng & Tín hiệu lộ trình

Yêu cầu tính năng mới hôm nay (tất cả đều có khả năng là ứng viên v0.9.0 trừ khi có ghi chú khác):

  • #11961 — Đăng nhập dashboard bằng OIDC (tùy chọn tham gia). PR #11965 đã mở → tín hiệu mạnh cho v0.9.0.
  • #11984 — Chat dashboard cho tài khoản đã đăng nhập không phải admin. Một phần của tracker #7432.
  • #11971 — Build source chỉ CLI (không gateway/dashboard). Đi kèm với PR #11975.
  • #11992 / #11799 — Template email cho operator + thân HTML được làm sạch; thông báo từ chối chính sách shell với lý do + gợi ý cho operator (PR #11983 mở).
  • #11995 — Khôi phục ủy quyền nền thuộc sở hữu với kết quả theo phạm vi principal (tiếp theo của #11409).
  • #11847 — Kênh XMPP/Prosody với OMEMO tùy chọn (PR tính năng, XL).

Dự đoán lộ trình: v0.9.0 sẽ tập trung vào (1) OIDC/danh tính & truy cập theo phạm vi principal, (2) đăng nhập dashboard + chat theo phạm vi, (3) bản build chỉ CLI/tối giản, và (4) hoàn thiện kênh email. Vòng đời tác vụ bền vững của Goal Mode (#11878, "proposal 1/12") báo hiệu một sáng kiến đa phát hành lớn hơn nhiều đang bắt đầu giai đoạn nền tảng.

7. Tóm tắt phản hồi người dùng

Điểm đau được nêu trong các issue:

  • Lo lắng về kiểm soát bảo mật — Người dùng (và chính nhóm maintainer) đang tìm ra nhiều cách mà principal theo phạm vi thoát khỏi ranh giới của mình: bypass allowlist của delegate (#8279), thực thi SOP không có quyền admin (#11220), công cụ dữ liệu phiên bị lộ cho người không phải admin (#11230), plugin chiếm trước công cụ (#11327). Chủ đề lặp lại là phạm vi danh tính tồn tại nhưng không được thực thi end-to-end.
  • Ma sát vòng đời plugin — #10999 bị kẹt ở blocked cho thấy operator gặp khó khăn để chứng minh một plugin cài đặt được từ artifact phát hành; #11357 (xóa nhầm thư mục) càng làm trầm trọng thêm vấn đề tin cậy.
  • Khoảng trống UX cho operator — #11799 ("từ chối chính sách shell nên nói lý do"), #11821 (bản ghi log không nêu tên người gửi bị từ chối), và #11972 (thoát 0 khi thất bại) cho thấy một mẫu hình: lỗi tồn tại nhưng không thể hành động được đối với operator.
  • Nhu cầu triển khai tối giản — #11971/#11969 phản ánh người dùng muốn bản build headless, không gateway mà không bị rò rỉ tính năng.
  • Chất lượng kênh email — Một cụm issue về email (#11989, #11991, #119

Bản tin này được tạo tự động bởi agents-radar tự động tạo.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-10-23

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-10-23 05:33 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-23

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw is operating at very high throughput today, with 500 issues and 500 PRs updated in the last 24 hours, reflecting a mature, heavily-trafficked project with an active maintainer and triage pipeline (clawsweeper bot) and a large self-hosted user base. Activity skews toward stability hardening rather than new capability: the issue queue is dominated by P0/P1 crash-loop, message-loss, and session-state regressions, while the PR queue is dominated by steipete and other maintainers folding single-consumer internal surfaces, fixing restart-recovery authority bugs, and improving UI/perf. The project shipped v2026.10.6, whose headline item is a mandatory Node runtime bump to patch a TLS certificate compromise — a security-driven forced upgrade. Net health signal: strong maintainer responsiveness, but a persistent backlog of long-lived platform-specific regressions (Windows, macOS sleep/wake) that keep resurfacing across releases.

2. Releases

v2026.10.6 — openclaw 2026.10.6

Highlight: Patched Node runtime is now required.

  • Breaking/enforced change: OpenClaw now requires Node 24.22.1+ (24 line) or 26.12.1+ (26 line). These runtimes reject TLS chains signed with the compromised certificate keys addressed in the October 2026 Node.js security releases.
  • Docker: official images now ship Node 24.2x (aligned to the patched line).
  • Migration note: Operators running older Node 24.x or 26.x builds must upgrade Node before installing this release, or TLS chains signed with compromised keys may still be accepted. This is a security-driven forced upgrade with no feature content described.

No other releases in the last 24h.

3. Project Progress

PR throughput: 259 PRs merged/closed in the last 24h vs. 241 still open — a healthy merge rate.

Notable merged/closed work visible today:

  • PR #181200 (closed) — fix(compaction): explain empty summary budget failures — improves operator error messaging when compaction summaries are length-stopped/empty. link
  • PR #177929 (closed) — fix(ui): Show earlier loses keyboard focus while older history loads — accessibility fix in Chat. link
  • PR #181191 (closed) — fix(control-ui): preserve in-flight MCP app setup — an experiment documenting 15–33 duplicate mcp.app.view requests per signed-in dashboard reload. link
  • PR #181351 (closed) — refactor: fold single-consumer entry and provider surfaces — internal cleanup across provider plugins, no user-visible change. link
  • PR #181176 (closed) — docs: explain plugin-owned database client error recovery — documents a hardening pattern after #146290 (plugin PG client error could terminate Gateway). link
  • Issue #148308 (closed) — Tailscale Serve claim loss after tailscaled restart. link
  • Issue #126836 (closed) — sessions.reset reporting success without creating a window. link
  • Issue #144678 (closed) — iOS manual Gateway host scheme bug. link

Themes advancing: restart-recovery correctness (PRs #181363, #181373, #181364), memory plugin authority for subagent/sessions_send sessions (PR #181359), and lazy-loading/perf cleanup in Control UI (PRs #181142, #181334, #181355).

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment volume:

  1. #160959 [OPEN, P0] — Gateway blocks for minutes while capturing large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression) — 43 comments. Event-loop stall of minutes at startup and on prepared-runtime republish. link

    • Need: Regressions in the plugin-generation capture path are the single loudest complaint. Users on large plugin trees are effectively blocked.

  2. #42475 [OPEN, P2] — Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level — 27 comments, 1 👍. link

    • Need: Operators want daily/monthly spend caps enforced before model dispatch, without external monitoring. Long-lived (filed 2026-03) and still a product-decision item.

  3. #53763 [CLOSED, P3] — Built-in headless browser for reliable web access — 18 comments. link

    • Need: Eliminate the fragile three-layer (user Chrome / third-party API) web-access dependency.

  4. #168955 [OPEN, P1] — Startup regression 2026.10.1: ready ~1030s vs ~410s (Windows); sidecars.control-ui-assets blocks 477s — 17 comments. link

    • Need: Windows startup is degraded ~2.5x, traced to an asset sidecar phase.

  5. #157531 [OPEN, P3] — 2026.9.7 Fixes Tracker — 17 comments. link

Analysis: Community energy is concentrated on performance of startup/runtime paths and operational guardrails (cost budgets, egress/secret substitution). The volume of P0 crash-loop issues suggests a user base running long-lived, high-agent-count deployments (e.g., #180690 with ~810 agents).

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity/impact among today's updates:

Issue Severity Impact Fix PR?
#160959 — Gateway blocks minutes on large plugin capture P0 Event-loop stall; crash-loop No new fix PR
#156712 — openclaw triage subprocess holds gateway-lifecycle lock, blocks restart P0 Release blocker No new fix PR
#48920 — Live Docs ahead of release (Heartbeat IsolatedSessions) P0 Docs/behavior mismatch No
#115642 — Billing cooldown outlives outage; ~5h fixed lockout P0 Auth/provider No
#158592 — Post sleep/wake: prepared runtime publication times out, all messages fail until restart P0 Message-loss No
#166634 — Late reclamation checkpoint failure leaves agent unavailable P0 Session-state/message-loss No
#168955 — Windows startup ~1030s regression P1 Crash-loop/slow No
#180690 — doctor --fix heap OOM at 6 GB on ~810-agent state; 3 passes, ~110 min P1 Crash-loop No
#140010 — Windows sleep/resume WebSocket reconnect fails 30–60s+ P1 Crash-loop No
#172837 — Codex nativeSubagentAssignments never removed after delivery gives up P1 Session-state/message-loss No (source-repro)
#145690 — Subagent completion releases runtime generation; next lane task fails in ~15ms, message dropped P1 Message-loss No
#160485 — Plugin load CPU-bound on module compilation; 3 channel plugins = 57.4s of 60s P1 Startup perf No
#167557 — Deferred plugin migration never converges (Linux/npm) P1 UX friction Shape clear
#166004 — Windows scheduled-task Gateway won't start; 2026.9.8 update rolls back P0 Release blocker No
#141413 — macOS app omits token for local Gateway using SecretRef P0 Auth No
#141615 — WebChat stuck "Authenticated profile verification is unavailable" wedges all RPCs P0 Release blocker Linked PR open

Notable patterns:

  • Windows is a recurring pain point: #168955, #140010, #157812, #166004, #155359 (SQLite write-transaction holds 5.9–33.2s past busy_timeout=5000ms).
  • Sleep/wake recovery is fragile on both macOS (#158592) and Windows (#140010).
  • Runtime-generation lifecycle bugs (#145690, #172837) are causing silent message drops in subagent/delegation flows.
  • Memory/DB schema migrations at scale (#180690) are OOM-prone.
  • Very few of these P0s have new fix PRs today — a maintainer-attention gap for crash-loop-class bugs.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Active feature requests and likely direction:

  1. #42475 — Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway (P2, product-decision). Strong operator demand; a natural fit for a future release given existing session-cost-usage.ts tracking.
  2. #180139 (PR, open) — Bundle the Knowledge memory plugin — evidence-backed memory plugin would ship with core, off by default. Strong roadmap signal toward first-class memory. link
  3. #71142 — Configurable Control UI upload size limit (currently hardcoded 5MB). link
  4. #71330 — Configurable memory promotion target file (currently hardcodes MEMORY.md, subject to 12KB bootstrap truncation). link
  5. #144306 — Deliver automations to a paired node (scheduled results as app notifications). link
  6. #138279 — Linux aarch64 companion builds (deb + AppImage). link
  7. #181375 (PR, open) — gateway lanes CLI for diagnostics.lanes RPC — operator-facing diagnostics polish; likely to land soon. link
  8. #80638 — Make MAX_OVERFLOW_COMPACTION_ATTEMPTS config-driven (currently hardcoded 3; each attempt is billable). link

Prediction for next release (2026.10.7+): bundled/logbook-adjacent plugin bundling (#180139), gateway diagnostics CLI (#181375), and continued restart-recovery correctness fixes (#181363/#181373/#181364). Cost-budget enforcement (#42475) is more likely a 2026.11 roadmap item given its long open status and product-decision tag.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (dissatisfaction):

  • Startup/performance at scale: Windows users report ~2.5x startup regression (#168955); plugin-heavy installs see minute-long event-loop stalls (#160959) and 57s plugin phases (#160485). Users with hundreds of agents hit OOM in doctor --fix (#180690).
  • Reliability of delegation/subagents: Multiple users report silent message drops when subagent runs complete and runtime generations are released (#145690, #172837) — a class of bug that erodes trust in autonomous operation.
  • Sleep/wake fragility: Laptop users (macOS + Windows) repeatedly lose Gateway connectivity for 30–60s+ after resume (#140010, #158592).
  • Secret/auth config friction: macOS app omits tokens with SecretRef (#141413); WebChat can wedge all RPCs on a stuck profile verification (#141615); ported internal context carrier leaks as a visible user-role turn on Teams (#136360).
  • Self-hosted autonomy blocked by approval loops: #151112 describes security/approval mechanisms turning owners into manual executors even after delegation.

Satisfaction/positive use cases:

  • Strong engagement around memory-core dreaming/QMD and lifecycle-aware curation (#112349, #87660) shows users investing deeply in long-term memory.
  • Rich ecosystem usage (browser plugin, google-meet, Node companion) shows adoption beyond the core chat loop.
  • High 👍 on some long-standing requests (#48920 has 4 👍) signals sustained interest rather than churn.

Net sentiment: Power users are committed but visibly taxed by platform-specific instability and by the operational cost of running OpenClaw at scale. The fastest satisfaction win would be hardening Windows startup and sleep/wake recovery.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-unanswered or high-importance items needing maintainer attention:

  • #42475 — Per-agent cost budgets. Open since 2026-03-10; 27 comments; tagged needs-product-decision. A clear product signal stuck without a decision. link
  • #48920 — Live Docs ahead of release (Heartbeat IsolatedSessions). P0, open since 2026-03-17; docs/release mismatch confuses users. link
  • #115642 — Billing cooldown outlives outage. P0, open since 2026-07-29; affects subscription auth users with a hard ~5h lockout. link
  • #155359 — Windows SQLite write-transaction holds past busy_timeout. P1, supersedes #154971; needs maintainer review. link
  • #157812 — Windows auto-update fails repeatedly (managed-service-preflight, unexpanded $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, reconcile:abandoned). P2, needs-info. link
  • #157531 — 2026.9.7 Fixes Tracker. Stale; a rolling tracker that may need closure or re-scoping. link
  • PR #119762 — feat(release): validate Windows-node releases and main. Open since 2026-08-05; waiting on author; would add needed Windows compatibility lanes. link
  • PR #75225 — feat(agents): expose configured descriptions in agents_list. Stale since 2026-04-30; proof supplied but awaiting maintainer decision. link
  • PR #173437 — fix(release): move validation waivers into trusted tooling. XL, needs proof, touches release/security boundaries. link

Health Assessment

  • Strengths: High maintainer cadence (259 PRs merged/closed in 24h), disciplined triage labeling (clawsweeper/impact/severity tags), and rapid security response (TLS-compromise Node bump in v2026.10.6).
  • Risks: A durable cluster of P0 crash-loop / message-loss regressions without attached fix PRs, concentrated on Windows, sleep/wake recovery, and runtime-generation lifecycle. If unaddressed, these will keep qualifying as release blockers and erode trust in autonomous operation at scale.
  • Opportunity: The backlog contains several near-ready wins (diagnostics CLI, memory CRUD fixes, UI perf/accessibility) and one high-consensus feature (cost budgets) that could materially improve operator confidence.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent Open-Source Ecosystem

Data window: 2026-10-23 | Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The five projects analyzed span a wide maturity spectrum — from OpenClaw's high-throughput, self-hosted flagship (~500 issues/PRs updated daily, mandatory security-driven runtime bump) to IronClaw's near-dormant maintenance window (8 total items, Dependabot-only PRs). Across the ecosystem, the dominant engineering theme in October 2026 is hardening over expansion: crash-loop/message-loss remediation on Windows and sleep/wake paths (OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw), identity/principal-scope enforcement in multi-tenant deployments (ZeroClaw), and channel-adapter reliability (QwenPaw, ZeroClaw). A secondary but persistent theme is memory governance — write-time budgets, promotion targets, and privacy boundaries — appearing independently in OpenClaw, Hermes, and QwenPaw. Security events (Node TLS compromise in OpenClaw; emSign CA in QwenPaw) drove two forced-upgrade releases in 24 hours, underscoring that supply-chain hygiene is now a first-class release concern.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues Updated (24h) PRs Updated (24h) Merge Rate (PRs merged/updated) Release Status (24h) Health Signal
OpenClaw 500 500 259 merged / 500 (≈52%) v2026.10.6 — mandated Node runtime bump (TLS compromise) Strong throughput; durable P0 backlog (Windows, sleep/wake, runtime-gen) without fix PRs
Hermes Agent 50 50 15 merged / 50 (30%); 0 issues closed v0.22.5 — rollup of ~81 PRs pre-v0.23.0 Feature momentum strong; release/update-path quality is the dominant risk
IronClaw 2 6 1 merged (superseded Dependabot) None Stable but low-velocity; maintenance-only; human contribution effectively paused
QwenPaw 22 50 2 merged / 50 (4%) v2.2.2.post1 — emSign CA security hotfix Responsive on security; severe PR review-bandwidth bottleneck; upgrade-regression cluster
ZeroClaw 34 50 8 merged/closed PRs; 11 issues closed None (pre-v0.9.0 stabilization) High volume; merge-throughput risk from stacked XL security PRs

Composite read: Only OpenClaw demonstrates a balanced high-volume pipeline. QwenPaw and ZeroClaw show high input volume with constrained output — a classic pre-major-release review bottleneck. Hermes is mid-cycle between stability patches. IronClaw is effectively idle on human-driven work.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers:

  • Throughput at scale: 500 issues + 500 PRs updated in 24h — roughly 10× Hermes and QwenPaw, and ~15× ZeroClaw. 259 merged PRs/24h is unmatched.
  • Disciplined triage infrastructure: Automated clawsweeper bot with impact/severity labeling yields a machine-parseable backlog — a maturity marker none of the peers match.
  • Release engineering cadence: Ships feature-named releases (v2026.10.6) with explicit migration notes, whereas Hermes defers curated notes to the next minor (v0.23.0) and QwenPaw/ZeroClaw are mid-cycle.
  • Ecosystem breadth: Browser plugin, google-meet, Node companion, Teams — wider integration surface than any peer.

Technical approach differences:

  • OpenClaw is the heaviest / most pluggable architecture in the set: plugin-generation capture, MCP app setup, prepared-runtime publication, gateway lanes, sidecar asset phases. This power is also its liability — the same plugin/capture complexity produces the P0 event-loop stalls (#160959) and Windows startup regressions (#168955) absent from leaner peers.
  • Hermes and QwenPaw share OpenClaw's gateway/plugin model but with fewer architectural layers; ZeroClaw trades breadth for a security-first principal-scoped design; IronClaw is a smaller Rust/Cranelift-based artifact.

Community size comparison:

  • OpenClaw is the clear category reference — its issue comment counts (43 on #160959, 27 on #42475) and long-lived operator threads indicate a large, self-hosted power-user base running hundreds of agents (e.g., ~810-agent deployments). Peers operate at ~1/10 the engaged population.
  • However, measured by reaction intensity, Hermes punches above its weight: #18715 carries 👍42, higher than any OpenClaw item in today's set — suggesting a smaller but more ideologically invested community.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Requirement Projects Specific Need
Memory governance / write-time budgets OpenClaw (#71330, #42475), Hermes (#135039, #116788), QwenPaw (#8376 PowerContext) Per-file promotion targets, write-time budget/acceptance pipelines, privacy boundaries preventing forbidden saves
Principal-scoped access & permission enforcement ZeroClaw (#8279, #11220, #11230, #11327), OpenClaw (#141413 SecretRef, #151112 approval loops) End-to-end identity scope — current implementations enforce only partially (delegate bypass, approval-loop-toil)

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Tier 1 — High-volume, mature, self-sustaining (OpenClaw):

  • Balanced merge pipeline (52% merge rate), automated triage, security-responsive releases.
  • Risk: durable P0 crash-loop class without attached fix PRs; Windows and sleep/wake consistently weakest links.

Tier 2 — High-velocity, pre-major-release, contributor-rich (Hermes, ZeroClaw, QwenPaw):

  • Hermes: Rapid iteration; 0 issues closed vs. 50 active means a growing backlog. Many bugs already have fix PRs — healthy feedback loop. v0.23.0 stabilization window.
  • ZeroClaw: Highest architectural ambition (event-sourced sessions, Goal Mode). Bottleneck is stacked XL security PRs refreshing daily without merge — an integration-sequencing problem, not a contribution problem.
  • QwenPaw: Strongest contributor health signal (first-time contributors landing XXXL PRs: #8376, #8345, #8328) but 4% PR merge rate is the ecosystem's sharpest review-bandwidth constraint. Oldest untouched request 57 days (#7339).

Tier 3 — Low-velocity / maintenance mode (IronClaw):

  • Dependabot-only activity; human contribution paused. The unanswered daily failure taxonomy (#8153) will accrue silent model-quality debt absent a triage owner. ARM64 closure without a visible merge (#3168) needs verification.

Rapidly iterating: Hermes (feature + fix), ZeroClaw (security architecture), QwenPaw (plugin architecture). Stabilizing: OpenClaw (stability hardening over capability), Hermes (pre-v0.23.0), ZeroClaw (pre-v0.9.0). Stalled: IronClaw.

7. Trend Signals — Value for AI Agent Developers

  1. Memory is becoming a governed subsystem, not a scratchpad. Three projects independently requested write-time budgets, promotion targets, and acceptance pipelines. Actionable: design memory with per-file budgets, injection-cost awareness (MEMORY.md enters every turn), and explicit user-consent boundaries before they become retrofits.

  2. Approval heuristics are a trust liability. Hermes #141346 (smart mode → deleted unsaved PowerPoint) and OpenClaw #151112 (owners turned into manual executors) bracket the problem from both sides. Actionable: implement a distinct destructive/OS-automation class requiring stricter confirmation than generic tool approval — "smart" must not mean "silent on irreversible actions."

  3. Identity enforcement must be end-to-end or it is theatre. ZeroClaw's recurring escapes (#8279, #11220, #11230, #11327) show scope is easy to declare and hard to enforce. Actionable: treat allowlist containment, sub-agent delegation, and channel routing as a single audit surface; verify scope at every dispatch, not just session creation.

  4. Update paths are a first-class reliability surface. Windows update failures in Hermes (every run) and QwenPaw (post-upgrade QQ breakage; schema mismatch), plus OpenClaw's forced Node bump, show the delivery mechanism is as fragile as the software. Actionable: versioned, self-healing, channel-aware updates with accurate version reporting are a competitive feature, not plumbing.

  5. Cross-platform parity (esp. Windows, sleep/wake) remains unsolved. Windows is over-represented in bug clusters across OpenClaw, Hermes, and QwenPaw. Actionable: add Windows + resume-from-sleep to CI lanes before they qualify as release blockers (see OpenClaw PR #119762).

  6. Federation is the next architectural frontier. Hermes #97681 (cross-gateway collaboration, top-commented) and ZeroClaw's multi-principal OIDC both point at federated personal agents with preserved owner autonomy. Actionable: treat identity/trust as the hard problem, not transport.

  7. Supply-chain hygiene is now release-critical. Two forced security upgrades in one 24h window (Node TLS, emSign CA). Actionable: pin patched runtimes, sign/verify installers, and prepare drop-in patch channels.

  8. Plugin architecture is under-specified as the primary extension surface. QwenPaw's one-theme-knob limitation (#8071) and ZeroClaw's plugin tool-name gate (#11327) show plugins lack a semantic contract. Actionable: define a descriptor/token layer and capability model before plugin counts grow.

  9. Emerging norm: AI-authored, evidence-backed issues. QwenPaw #8078 carries an explicit AI-disclosure notice with reproducible local evidence — a governance pattern worth adopting as agent-generated issue volume rises.

Bottom line for decision-makers: The ecosystem's competitive axis is shifting from capability breadth (OpenClaw's historical strength) toward trustworthiness — enforced scope, governed memory, safe approvals, and durable updates. Projects that treat these as first-class subsystems (ZeroClaw's security-first posture; Hermes's responsive fix-PR loop) are best positioned for the enterprise/team deployments that QwenPaw and ZeroClaw are already courting.

Prediction: v2.3.0 will ship the plugin/channel extraction (#8187, #8289) as its headline. The theme extension point (#8071) is the most likely rider, since it is cheap once the plugin descriptor format is settled. Hub globalization (#8275) is the strongest candidate for 2.4.0.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points, by theme:

  • Upgrade anxiety is real and recurring. Multiple reports tie breakage directly to upgrading: QQ channel dead after 2.2.2 (#8388, missing _qwenpaw_remote_backend), model invocation failing from legacy agent.json (#8378). Combined with the forced security upgrade advisory (#8385), users are being asked to upgrade into a version with its own regressions. This is the sharpest satisfaction risk in the dataset.
  • Silent failures erode trust. DingTalk drops final replies with no error (#8343); Telegram silently discards quoted context (#8329); approvals raised from a chat never reach that chat and resolve to TIMEOUT after five minutes (PR #8303 describes the WeChat case). Users cannot distinguish "agent chose not to respond" from "system failed."
  • Resource exhaustion blocks work. The 48.9 MB WeChat body (#8335) and the Feishu network-stall-holds-the-whole-service (#8350) both render the product completely unusable, not merely degraded.
  • Team/Hub users feel like second-class citizens. Hub timeout too short (#8372), Hub-in-Docker deployment broken (#8359), no shared Skill/MCP (#8275).
  • Positive signals: Contributors are investing real effort — first-time contributors submitted substantial PRs (#8376 XXXL PowerContext, #8345 plugin loader robustness, #8328 offline Docker image), and maintainers publish transparent roadmap threads (#8289) with preliminary test results.

Notable AI-authored issue: #8078 carries an explicit AI-disclosure notice stating the built-in assistant helped investigate and write the report, with reproducible local evidence. This is an emerging community norm worth watching.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention due to age, severity, or lack of response:

  1. #7339 — Desktop auto-scroll toggle. Open since 2026-08-27 (~57 days), only 2 comments, no movement. This is a simple UX toggle that long-lived streaming users clearly want; it is the oldest untouched request in the dataset.
  2. #8071 — Plugin theme extension point. Open since 2026-10-01, 7 comments (the highest-engagement issue today) and actively discussed, but no maintainer commitment or PR. It risks stalling the 2.3.0 plugin story if not scoped soon.
  3. #8078 — Cross-session chat_with_agent messages registered as independent chats, splitting one session across multiple UI pages. Open since 2026-10-02, well-evidenced, no fix PR. This is a correctness issue in session modeling, not cosmetics.
  4. #8275 — Global Skill/MCP management. Open since 2026-10-16 with a 👍 but no maintainer reply; it is the anchor request for the entire team-deployment persona.
  5. PR #8187 (size/XXXL) — The channel extraction PR has been open since 2026-10-12 (11 days) and is the critical path for 2.3.0. An XXXL PR aging without merge increases rebase risk and contributor discouragement.
  6. PR #8243 / PR #8244 — Both marked Under Review since 2026-10-14 (Windows log rotation; channel SDK lazy-loading with a measured 15.1s startup win). The startup performance fix in particular has quantified benefit and is still waiting.

Health assessment: The project is responsive on security (same-week hotfix) but slow on feature PR throughput — 48 open PRs against 2 merged is a review-bandwidth bottleneck. The channel-layer bug cluster and the upgrade-regression reports are the two areas most likely to damage user trust if the 2.3.0 release ships without addressing them.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-23

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw shows high-velocity development activity with 34 issues and 50 PRs updated in the last 24 hours. The project is in an intense pre-release push toward v0.9.0, with the vast majority of new work carrying that milestone tag. The activity is heavily skewed toward security hardening and identity/access control — principal-scoped delegation, OIDC dashboard sign-in, session ownership, and tool allowlist containment dominate both the issue tracker and PR queue. No releases shipped today; the team appears to be stabilizing v0.8.7 fixes (plugins, OIDC, CI) while staging v0.9.0 features.

Health assessment: Active and healthy on contribution volume, but the concentration of high-risk, interdependent security PRs (many risk:high, size:XL, blocked on prerequisites) represents a merge-throughput risk.

2. Releases

None. No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Project Progress

Merged / Closed PRs Today (8 total)

No merged PRs appear in the top-20-by-comment sample (all visible PRs are OPEN). The 8 merged/closed PRs are lower-engagement items not surfaced in the data.

Closed Issues Today (11 total) — Notable closures

  • #10526 — RFC: Append-only session event history, deterministic state replay, and derived agent streams (13 comments, closed after ~7 weeks). This is a significant architectural milestone: an accepted RFC governing event-sourced session state that underpins much of the runtime roadmap.
  • #11357 — plugin remove deleted the wrong directory (plugins_dir/<name> instead of the load path). Security-relevant plugin lifecycle fix landed.
  • #11327 — Plugin tool-name gate could let a plugin pre-empt tool_search, MCP, peripheral and skill tools. Closed — relevant to the #8279 allowlist concern.

Takeaway: Today's closures are predominantly v0.8.7 stabilization and security/CI hygiene, while v0.9.0 features remain in-flight.

4. Community Hot Topics

Item Type Comments Theme
#7432 Tracker (p2, high risk) 15 Runtime / dashboard sign-in / gateway delivery roadmap
#10526 RFC (p2, high risk) 13 Event-sourced session history & deterministic replay
#10999 Task blocked (medium) 9 Discord plugin install/verify from release binary

  • #7432 is the master coordination issue for the v0.9.0 runtime/gateway release — its 15-comment thread signals ongoing sequencing debate and a large dependency graph. Stakeholders want clarity on what ships in v0.9.0.

Most-commented PRs are the security stack by IftekharUddin and Aarlington (#11225 p0, #11409, #11220, #11230, #11234) and the Goal Mode foundation #11878 — these drive the visible roadmap.

Stability read: Two sandbox/security-escape-class bugs remain open (#11823, #11991) with no fix PR — these warrant priority. The #11957 enrollment bug is S1 (workflow blocked) but a fix is already in review. TLS WebSocket breakage (#11951) is a regression-shaped issue affecting dashboard usability.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

New feature requests today (all likely v0.9.0 candidates unless noted):

  • #11961 — Dashboard sign-in with OIDC (opt-in). PR #11965 already open → strongly signaled for v0.9.0.

The Goal Mode durable task lifecycle (#11878, "proposal 1/12") signals a much larger multi-release initiative beginning its foundation phase.

Pain points expressed in issues:

The recurring theme is that identity scope exists but is not enforced end-to-end.

Satisfaction signals: Discord plugin (#10999) confirmed working on the published v0.8.6 archive — positive validation of the plugin pipeline despite the "prove it from release" gate.

8. Backlog Watch

Items needing maintainer attention:

  • #8279 — S0/p1 delegate allowlist bypass, open since 2026-06-24 (~4 months). Fix depends on a deep stacked PR chain still unmerged. Highest-risk outstanding security item.

  • #11951 — TLS WebSocket regression blocking dashboard chat, no fix PR.

  • #11068 — Channel turns narrowed by sender role, open since 2026-09-23, needs-author-action, risk:high.
  • Stacked security PRs #11225 (p0), #11220, #11230, #11234 — All open ~3.5 weeks, refreshing daily, blocked on one another. This stack is the single biggest merge-throughput bottleneck for the v0.9.0 security story and needs maintainer sequencing decisions.
  • #11737 — Restore principal-owned Chat sessions after restart, marked draft, blocked on integration, with merge conflicts against master.
